title: What is boxing and unboxing in C#?
description: Understand value type to reference type conversions in .NET.

data.text: **Question:** What is boxing and unboxing in C#?
Boxing converts a value type to a reference type (object). Unboxing converts it back. Both operations involve heap allocation and type checking, which have performance costs.

**Boxing:**
- Converts value type to reference type
- Allocates memory on heap
- Copies value from stack to heap
- Implicit conversion
- Example: int i = 10; object obj = i;
- Performance overhead: allocation + copy

**Unboxing:**
- Converts reference type back to value type
- Requires explicit cast
- Checks type compatibility at runtime
- Throws InvalidCastException if wrong type
- Example: int j = (int)obj;
- Performance overhead: type check + copy

**Performance Impact:**
- Boxing creates garbage (heap allocation)
- Unboxing requires runtime type check
- Both are expensive in tight loops
- Avoid in performance-critical code
- Use generics to avoid boxing
